resources.string: Switching works while the other device is playing something.
Ruru only moves the sound between devices. It never removes or forgets one. To pair or remove a device, use your system's Bluetooth settings.
The headphones can't switch yet. Start playing audio on the other device, then try again.
Swipe and tap the ear cup for volume, pause and skip
Plays a rising tone, quiet at first and louder over a few seconds. It stops by itself after %1$d seconds.
The tone comes out of your system's sound output, so choose the headphones as the output first, and take them off before you start.
The tone goes to the headphones only. Take them off before you start.
Playing. Don't put the headphones on until you stop it.
Records %1$d seconds from the microphone, then plays it back, so you hear what the other person hears on a call. Nothing is saved.
While it records, Windows switches the headphones to call quality, so the sound gets thinner for a moment. Choose the headphones as the input in your sound settings first.
While it records, your system may switch the headphones to call quality, so the sound gets thinner for a moment. Choose the headphones as the input in your sound settings first.
While it records, your phone switches the headphones to call quality, so the sound gets thinner for a moment.
Done. Start it again to hear another.
Waiting for your answer about the microphone.
Ruru can't play sound on this system right now.
Ruru can't use the microphone. Check that no other app is using it and that Ruru is allowed to in your privacy settings.
The mic check needs permission to use the microphone. You can allow it in your phone's settings.
Android isn't sending sound to the headphones right now, so the tone would come from the phone. Play something on the headphones first, then try again.
